items.text: That is the part that should actually drive your decision.
A quiz result or a single personality label will not settle this.
You get satisfaction from a piece looking exactly right, the right typeface, the right spacing, the right colour story, and from that piece existing as a complete, shippable thing once it is done.
If "the design changed because the data said so" feels like progress rather than a loss, that instinct fits UI/UX better than graphic design.
This is the part most head-to-head comparisons skip entirely, and it is often the most useful answer for someone who genuinely likes parts of both fields.

The overlap is not a vague hybrid title, it is a real, growing set of roles inside Indian startups, agencies, and product teams that specifically need someone who can design a strong visual identity and also think about how a screen actually gets used.
Owns both the visual identity and the product screens for a smaller company or startup that cannot yet afford separate specialists.

blocks.heading: Mistakes to Avoid When Making This Decision

items.text: Average salary comparisons hide the spread.
Running a Canva template and building a coherent brand system that a client trusts for years are not the same skill.
The core tool (Figma) is learnable in weeks, which means the market has plenty of certificate-holders with near-identical, unresearched case studies.

blocks.heading: Static Visual Assets Logos
rows: Core daily task
Design static visual assets: logos, brand identity, packaging, social creatives, print collateral, or marketing decks. Work is briefed, designed, revised, and shipped as a finished visual file.

Research how people use a product, then wireframe, prototype, and design screens for an app or website. Work is designed, tested with real users, and revised based on what the test shows, not just personal taste.
Where the day gets hard
A client or brand manager wants three rounds of "make it pop" revisions with no clear direction, or a print deadline collides with a last-minute logo change.
A usability test reveals your favourite screen confuses real users, and you have to rework a flow you were proud of based on evidence, not opinion.
Main tools
Adobe Photoshop, Illustrator, InDesign, and increasingly Canva or AI image tools for faster asset production.
Figma (now the near-universal industry standard), plus research and testing tools like Maze, Hotjar, or UserTesting, and light prototyping in tools like ProtoPie for complex interactions.
Who you talk to most
Brand managers, marketing teams, print vendors, and clients, mostly conversations about look, feel, and brand consistency.
Product managers, developers, and actual users in research sessions, mostly conversations about what a user needs and whether the design actually solves it.
How your work gets judged
Visual quality and brand fit, judged fairly quickly by a creative director, client, or marketing lead, the feedback loop is short.
Usability metrics, task completion rates, and business outcomes like conversion or retention, judged over weeks through testing and product data, the feedback loop is longer but more evidence-based.

blocks.heading: Learning Curve and Entry Barrier
rows: What "job-ready" actually requires

A tight portfolio of finished visual work, logos, branding projects, social or print campaigns, that shows range and consistency. Craft and taste are judged almost entirely by the eye, so the portfolio has to look genuinely professional, not just competent.

A case-study portfolio that shows your process: the problem, the research, the wireframes, the testing, and the final design with reasoning. Employers hire the thinking behind the screens as much as the screens themselves.
Typical time to interview-ready from zero

Many people build a presentable starter portfolio in a focused stretch of a few months, since the core tools (Photoshop, Illustrator) have a shorter learning curve and visual taste can be practiced through repetition.

Most structured paths estimate roughly four to six months of consistent study to reach a credible first case study, because the skill stack (research methods, information architecture, Figma, prototyping, and writing up a case study) is wider than one tool.
Formal degree dependency
Low. A design diploma or fine-arts background helps but is not required, hiring managers in agencies and studios weigh the portfolio far more than the degree.

Low to moderate. No specific degree is required, and many working UI/UX designers come from graphic design, psychology, or even engineering backgrounds, but candidates with zero research or IA training face a steeper self-taught curve.
What makes the entry filter hard
The market is saturated with visually competent generalists, so pure taste and speed increasingly need to be paired with a niche (packaging, motion, brand systems) to stand out.

The title is hyped enough that many bootcamp graduates apply with template-based case studies that look similar to a hundred others; a real, evidence-based case study with actual user testing behind it is what actually clears the interview bar.

blocks.heading: Without the Marketing Numbers
rows: Fresher, 0-1 years
Roughly Rs 2-4 LPA, with high competition and low specialisation keeping the entry band narrow compared to product design roles.
Roughly Rs 2.5-7 LPA, with a strong case-study portfolio and demonstrated research skill pushing candidates toward the top of that range.
3-5 years experience
Roughly Rs 5-8 LPA, especially for designers who have added digital marketing, motion, or brand-strategy skill on top of core visual craft.
Roughly Rs 8-15 LPA, with designers who can run research independently and speak the language of product metrics moving toward the top of the band.
5+ years, senior
Roughly Rs 8-15 LPA for senior graphic designers or art directors in strong agencies and brand teams; the ceiling is usually reached through creative leadership, not further craft depth alone.
Roughly Rs 18-30+ LPA for senior UI/UX designers, product design leads, and design managers, particularly in Bengaluru, Hyderabad, and Pune tech and SaaS hubs.
What moves the number most
A visible, differentiated style plus business skill, designers who understand branding strategy and marketing outcomes, not just visuals, earn more than pure "make it pretty" generalists.
Proof that your design decisions changed a real metric (conversion, retention, task completion), combined with comfort speaking directly to product and engineering teams.

blocks.heading: Real Career Growth Ceiling in Each Field
rows: Typical promotion ladder
Junior designer to senior designer to art director to creative head, or a parallel move into brand strategy, marketing leadership, or running your own studio.
Junior/associate designer to UX designer to senior designer to design lead to head of design or VP of design, with a well-defined corporate ladder inside most tech and product companies.
Ceiling driven by
Creative reputation, client relationships, and the ability to lead a creative team or build a personal brand or studio, growth depends heavily on individual visibility.
Ability to tie design decisions to measurable product outcomes, plus cross-functional influence with product and engineering, growth is more structurally built into the org chart of tech companies.
India-specific demand signal
Steady, broad demand, every business with a brand needs graphic design, but supply is high too, since the entry skill bar is comparatively lower and more people compete for the same roles.

Design leaders report demand has increased or held steady across roughly 82% of organisations, with double-digit growth in several sectors, and tens of thousands of active listings across product, SaaS, fintech, and e-commerce companies.
Independent income path
Well-worn and common, freelance branding work, running a small design studio, or building a personal client base is a realistic path once you have 3-4 strong projects to show.

Realistic but requires a wider skill set to sell solo, freelance and consulting UI/UX work exists and pays well per hour, but it usually needs more years of in-house experience first to build credibility with clients who cannot easily judge research quality themselves.

blocks.heading: Freelance Viability: Which One Pays Better Solo
rows: Typical India hourly rate
Roughly Rs 500-1,500/hour for freshers and mid-level freelancers, rising toward Rs 2,500-3,000/hour for experienced brand and packaging specialists.
Roughly Rs 2,500-7,000/hour for experienced freelancers, reflecting the narrower pool of designers who can credibly run research and deliver tested product screens, not just visuals.
How clients find and vet you
Visually, a client can judge a graphic design portfolio in seconds, which makes cold outreach and marketplace listings (Fiverr, Behance, Instagram) a realistic acquisition channel.

Less visually, more by reputation and referral, a non-technical client often cannot judge whether your research method was sound, so trust usually comes through referrals, case studies, or a track record with similar products.
Repeat-client potential
High for ongoing brand or marketing work, a business needs new social creatives, ads, and collateral constantly, which supports recurring freelance income.

Project-based and less naturally recurring, most products need a UI/UX overhaul or a defined feature project rather than continuous weekly design work, so freelance UI/UX income is often lumpier unless you build a retainer relationship.
Realistic first-client path
A small business needing a logo, social kit, or one-off campaign is an easy, low-friction first client to find through marketplaces or local networks.

A startup founder needing a defined MVP screen set or a redesign sprint is a realistic first client, but usually requires a stronger portfolio and a warmer introduction than graphic design freelancing does.
